fields.title: Ebola Outbreak, DRC and Region, Situation Report #12 (August 19, 2026)
fields.body:
**FAST FACTS**

- On May 15, the DRC declared an outbreak of Ebola virus disease (EVD), later confirmed to be caused by the Bundibugyo strain.
- As of August 18, 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 confirmed deaths had been reported in the DRC, with 20 confirmed cases and two confirmed deaths in Uganda.
- In the DRC, the outbreak remains centered in Ituri province, but cases have also been confirmed in Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo provinces.
- In Uganda, the last confirmed case was discharged on July 16.
- No EVD cases have been confirmed in South Sudan, but risk of an outbreak remains high due to transient populations and porous borders with the DRC.

**OUR RESPONSE**

- Across the region, our teams are providing case management, infection prevention and control (IPC), screening and triage, risk communication and community engagement, training and preparedness planning.
- We are supporting 162 facilities in the screening, identification and treatment of EVD.
- Our supported sites have conducted 376,857 screenings and provided treatment to 1,374 patients, including 377 confirmed cases.
- We have so far trained 2,820 people in the DRC on EVD case management, response and transmission prevention.

With the support of the US Department of State, DG ECHO and other donors, International Medical Corps teams are actively responding to the outbreak across the region while collaborating closely with ministries of health, key actors and response partners. International Medical Corps has used a hub-and-spoke model since the outbreak was declared, providing case-management support at designated treatment and transit facilities, strengthening IPC in referring health facilities, conducting screening and triage, supporting risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) in surrounding communities and training health workers on EVD response protocols.

In the DRC, International Medical Corps is running three Ebola Treatment Centers (including one that is the country's largest) and seven Ebola transit centers. We continue to closely coordinate with the MoH and relevant partners to support case management, screening-and-referral units, facility-based surveillance, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), IPC, logistics, just-in-time training, continuity of essential health services, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. International Medical Corps also is part of broader efforts to expand contact tracing, helping to strengthen mapping, daily monitoring and follow-up activities to address the risk of undetected transmission across operational areas and beyond.

In Uganda, we are working through a partner to to strengthen Ebola preparedness, surveillance, IPC, WASH, and RCCE activities across Ntoroko and Bundibugyo districts. We continue to support EVD national preparedness in South Sudan, where no cases have yet been confirmed, by upgrading and expanding infectious-disease units, training health staff and managing suspected cases.

fields.title: Commission Mouvement de Population Rapport - 31 Juillet 2026
fields.body:
I. Introduction  
La Commission Mouvement de Population (CMP) est un mécanisme inter-organisationnel qui a pour but de fournir mensuellement des statistiques précises et d’analyser les tendances des déplacements forcés de populations en RCA. Cette tâche implique l’examen, la compilation et la consolidation des informations recueillies par les CMP locales et par les partenaires opérant dans les zones non couvertes par une CMP. Le rapport s’appuie sur des données issues de diverses sources, dont le CCCM, la DTM et le monitoring de la protection, ainsi que des évaluations alertes et des rapports de mission relatifs aux mouvements de population. La CMP effectue d’abord une validation préliminaire des données au niveau national, puis les transmet à l’Équipe Humanitaire Pays (EHP) pour approbation définitive.  
Le suivi des déplacements internes demeure un élément essentiel pour orienter la réponse humanitaire et soutenir la prise de décision opérationnelle en République Centrafricaine (RCA). Dans un contexte marqué par des mouvements de populations liés aux conflits, aux tensions communautaires, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux chocs socio-économiques, la disponibilité d'informations actualisées sur les personnes déplacées internes (PDI) constitue un préalable indispensable à une planification efficace des interventions.  
Le présent rapport s'appuie sur les données collectées dans le cadre du suivi de mouvements de PDI et présente une analyse de la situation des PDI entre avril et juillet 2026, en comparaison avec les données de référence de mars 2026. L'exercice vise à mettre en évidence les principales tendances observées, les évolutions des effectifs, ainsi que les dynamiques géographiques du déplacement interne à travers le pays1.

fields.title: Operational Update - Central African Republic - April - June 2026
fields.body: UNHCR's operations in the Central African Republic (CAR) are based on protection through presence, a central pillar of the humanitarian response. In a context marked by security volatility and the repercussions of the Sudanese crisis, particular attention is also being paid to emergency response. At the same time, the search for durable solutions is a major priority, by supporting the voluntary, safe and dignified return of Central African refugees, while ensuring their sustainable reintegration and their contribution to national development. The Central African Government, UNHCR and partners are providing protection and multi-sectoral assistance to internally displaced persons (IDPs) and refugees, including Chadians and Sudanese, while promoting durable solutions for Central African returnees. UNHCR aligns its interventions with national priorities, including the National Development Programme, the National Strategy for Durable Solutions and the Platform to Support Solutions from the 2022 Yaoundé Declaration.

fields.title: UNICEF Democratic Republic of the Congo Humanitarian Situation Report No. 2 – Ebola Outbreak (Bundibugyo Virus), 31 July 2026
fields.body:
**Highlights**

- UNICEF is scaling up its response from 21 to over 50 affected and high-risk health zones, supporting Government-led efforts across community-based surveillance, RCCE, IPC/WASH, nutrition, MHPSS, clinical care, PSEA and continuity of essential services.
- UNICEF-supported community surveillance networks generated 15,927 alerts in July, following the deployment and support of 6,009 community mobilizers since the start of the response, strengthening early detection, alert reporting, contact tracing, and community-level surveillance capacities across affected areas.
- UNICEF and partners reached over 1.4 million people with Ebola prevention and response messages through direct interpersonal communication approaches including door-to-door outreach, focused discussions, and community dialogues during this reporting period, while community feedback and social listening mechanisms continued to inform adaptive response strategies and address rumours and misinformation.
- UNICEF and partners continued to deliver integrated support for children and families, including MHPSS services for 12,780 children, adolescents and caregivers, case management for 407 Ebola-affected children, and treatment for 6,587 children with severe or moderate acute malnutrition.
- UNICEF supported the procurement of US$6.3 million worth of essential Ebola response supplies, including PPE, IPC materials and medical commodities, to sustain life-saving response operations across affected and high-risk health zones.
- UNICEF requires US$113.5 million for its revised six-month response plan. As of 31 July 2026, US$32.7 million had been mobilized, leaving a US$80.8 million funding gap, equivalent to 71 per cent of the requirement.

fields.title: WFP Chad Country Brief, August 2026
fields.body:
**SITUATION OVERVIEW**

• Between June and September 2026, crisis levels of acute food insecurity (IPC 3) are expected in Chad’s eastern provinces that host Sudanese refugees, as well as in the western Lake Province, which has a large internally displaced population due to persistent attacks by armed groups, according to FEWS NET’s latest analysis. The analysis highlights that refugees – more than 940,610 people who have arrived since the outbreak of the Sudan crisis in April 2023 (UNHCR) – have lost access to their livelihoods, have very limited sources of income, and must compete with host communities for scarce agricultural and nonagricultural employment opportunities. As a result, refugees rely heavily on food assistance to meet their basic food needs. In Lake Province, worsening insecurity has led to the abandonment of arable land, population displacement, and a decline in fishing activities. As a consequence, an estimated 75,000 people have been displaced since May 2026, adding to an already severe humanitarian situation affecting nearly 220,000 IDPs, as well as returnees and refugees.

fields.title: Afrique de l’Ouest et centrale : Derniers événements en bref (du 11 au 17 août 2026)
fields.body:
**Cameroun**  
*Le CERF alloue 1 million de dollars pour lutter contre les inondations qui aggravent les risques de choléra dans la région de l'Extrême-Nord*  
 Le Fonds central d’intervention d’urgence (CERF) a alloué 1 million de dollars pour soutenir la prévention du choléra, le traitement ainsi que les services d’approvisionnement en eau potable et d’assainissement pour 230 000 personnes, en particulier les enfants, les réfugiés et les communautés frontalières à haut risque. Au 12 août, 1 252 cas et 31 décès avaient été signalés dans neuf districts sanitaires. De fortes pluies et des vents violents ont également touché 742 personnes dans six localités du Logone et Chari, endommageant 257 habitations, 17 écoles et huit points d'eau.

Les inondations sont particulièrement préoccupantes à Makary, le deuxième district de choléra le plus touché de la région, et pourraient encore accroître la transmission à mesure que la saison des pluies s’intensifie. Dans le camp de réfugiés de Minawao, qui accueille plus de 81 000 réfugiés, 80 cas ont été enregistrés. Le Plan de réponse et de besoins humanitaires de 319 millions de dollars pour 2026 est financé à un peu plus de 25 pour cent.

**République centrafricaine**  
*L'ONU soutient les efforts de préparation et de prévention contre Ebola*

Bien qu’aucun cas d’Ebola n’ait été signalé en République centrafricaine, les Nations Unies soutiennent la préparation nationale compte tenu de la longue frontière du pays avec la République démocratique du Congo. Un mécanisme de coordination interinstitutions dirigé par l'OMS et le Département de la sûreté et de la sécurité des Nations Unies surveille les développements et aide le gouvernement en matière de surveillance, de conseils techniques, de communication sur les risques, de sensibilisation de la communauté et de renforcement des capacités.

La mission de maintien de la paix des Nations Unies transporte également des experts de la santé, livre des équipements et des fournitures essentiels et diffuse des messages hebdomadaires de santé publique en sango via Guira FM pour promouvoir les mesures préventives et lutter contre la désinformation.

**République démocratique du Congo**  
*L'ONU intensifie sa réponse à l'épidémie d'Ebola qui s'étend rapidement*

Le 14 août, le coordinateur des secours d’urgence, Tom Fletcher, a averti que l’épidémie d’Ebola en République démocratique du Congo prenait le pas sur la réponse humanitaire, avec plus de 2 000 décès signalés et un décès toutes les 30 minutes. À l’issue d’une réunion d’urgence du Comité permanent interorganisations, les responsables humanitaires ont convenu de renforcer l’action collective. M. Fletcher a alloué 30,5 millions de dollars supplémentaires provenant du CERF, venant s’ajouter à une précédente allocation de 24 millions de dollars destinée à ce pays et à quatre pays voisins, et a déployé 20 personnes supplémentaires sur le terrain.

Cette intensification des efforts visera principalement à généraliser les enterrements sûrs et dignes, à augmenter la capacité de traitement, à améliorer la recherche des contacts et à renforcer l’accès à l’eau, à l’assainissement, à l’hygiène, aux soins de santé et à d’autres services essentiels. Près de 300 millions de dollars ont été fournis par des donateurs internationaux pour soutenir cette intervention.

**Sahel central**  
*Le forum humanitaire adopte la Déclaration de Ouagadougou*

Le 12 août, le deuxième forum humanitaire ministériel de l’Alliance des États du Sahel s’est conclu par des recommandations visant à renforcer la coopération, la coordination et la réponse d’urgence humanitaires. La Déclaration appelle à des liens plus étroits entre l’action humanitaire, le relèvement, la résilience et l’inclusion sociale, en mettant l’accent sur une mise en œuvre concrète et mesurable.

Dans les trois pays, 12,6 millions de personnes ont besoin d'assistance, tandis que les plans d'intervention sont financés à hauteur de seulement 28 pour cent au Burkina Faso, 20 pour cent au Mali et 16 pour cent au Niger.

fields.title: West and Central Africa: Latest Events at a glance (11–17 August 2026)
fields.body:
**Cameroon**  
*CERF allocates $1 million as flooding compounds cholera risks in Far North Region*

The Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) allocated US$1 million to support cholera prevention, treatment, and safe water and sanitation services for 230,000 people, particularly children, refugees and high-risk border communities. As of 12 August, 1,252 cases and 31 deaths had been reported across nine health districts. Heavy rains and strong winds also affected 742 people in six localities in Logone et Chari, damaging 257 homes, 17 schools and eight water points.

Flooding is particularly concerning in Makary, the region’s second-most affected cholera district, and could further increase transmission as the rainy season intensifies. In Minawao refugee camp, which hosts more than 81,000 refugees, 80 cases have been recorded. The $319 million 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan is just over 25 per cent funded.

**Central African Republic**  
*UN supports Ebola preparedness and prevention efforts*

Although no Ebola cases have been reported in the Central African Republic, the United Nations is supporting national preparedness given the country’s long border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. An inter-agency coordination mechanism led by WHO and the UN Department of Safety and Security is monitoring developments and assisting the Government with surveillance, technical guidance, risk communication, community awareness and capacity-building.

The UN peacekeeping mission is also transporting health experts, delivering essential equipment and supplies, and broadcasting weekly public health messages in Sango through radio to promote preventive measures and counter misinformation.

**Democratic Republic of the Congo**  
*UN scales up response to rapidly growing Ebola outbreak*

On 14 August, Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was outpacing the humanitarian response, with more than 2,000 deaths reported and one person dying every 30 minutes. Following an emergency meeting of the Inter-Agency Standing Committee, humanitarian leaders agreed to accelerate collective action. Fletcher allocated an additional US$30.5 million from the CERF, complementing an earlier $24 million allocation to the country and four neighbouring countries, and deployed 20 additional personnel to frontline operations.

The scale-up will focus on expanding safe and dignified burials, tripling treatment capacity, improving contact tracing and strengthening access to water, sanitation, hygiene, health care and other essential services. Nearly $300 million has been provided by international donors to support the response.

**Central Sahel**  
*Humanitarian forum adopts Ouagadougou Declaration*

On 12 August, the second ministerial humanitarian forum of the Alliance of Sahel States concluded with recommendations to strengthen humanitarian cooperation, coordination and emergency response. The Declaration calls for closer links between humanitarian action, recovery, resilience and social inclusion, with an emphasis on concrete and measurable implementation.

Across the three countries, 12.6 million people require assistance, while response plans are funded at only 28 per cent in Burkina Faso, 20 per cent in Mali and 16 per cent in Niger.

fields.title: Note d’analyse: Province du Lac — Situation sanitaire sous la pression des déplacements de population (18 août 2026)
fields.body:
**Synthèse analytique**

- **Un choc capacitaire diffus :** l'impact des déplacements dépasse le cadre de la réponse au choléra et touche l'ensemble des services de santé courants (vaccination, soins primaires, référencement).
- **Une dépendance structurelle aux partenaires :** l'essentiel des ressources humaines qualifiées et des capacités d'approvisionnement repose sur des acteurs dont l'engagement est sensible aux cycles de financement, sans filet de sécurité étatique local.
- **Des indicateurs à fiabiliser :** la sous-estimation démographique des populations déplacées fragilise la lecture des performances sanitaires (vaccination notamment) et donc le pilotage de la réponse.
- **Une vulnérabilité qui précède et prolonge toute épidémie :** les mêmes fragilités (RH, approvisionnement, chaîne du froid, référencement) qui compliquent la réponse au choléra continueront de peser sur le système de santé une fois l'épidémie maîtrisée, si elles ne sont pas traitées pour elles-mêmes.

fields.title: Central African Republic hosts cross-border consultation on the risk of Bundibugyo virus disease
fields.body:
Bangui – A high-level cross-border meeting opened on Friday, 14 August 2026, in Bangui, Central African Republic, to strengthen preparedness and coordination in response to the risks posed by Bundibugyo virus disease. Convened by the World Health Organization (WHO), the meeting brings together the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, South Sudan and Uganda, to strengthen regional cooperation in addressing the threat of Bundibugyo virus disease and other cross-border health emergencies.

As part of efforts to harmonize alert mechanisms, strengthen surveillance at points of entry, and engage border communities in preparedness and response, the participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to working together on joint actions that transcend administrative boundaries.

“It is essential that our countries work closely together, pooling our efforts and collective wisdom, particularly along our shared borders, where communities exchange not only goods but also maintain family ties rooted in shared cultures and traditions,” said Central African Republic Prime Minister Félix Moloua.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo declared an outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease on 15 May 2026. Three months later, more than 4,300 cases had been confirmed in the country, including more than 2,000 deaths. Against this background, Baltasar Engonga Edjo'o, President of the Commission of the Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa (CEMAC), warned of the continued threat posed by Ebola. “Central Africa is well aware of the human, economic and social risks posed by the spread of the virus,” he said, noting that the Commission had already mobilized a subregional technical group and adopted a regional roadmap to intensify surveillance and strengthen security measures at points of entry.

“Viruses do not stop at borders,” said WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, underscoring the importance of a collective approach to investing in preparedness. “When one country prepares, Africa becomes stronger. Our borders may separate our countries, but they cannot divide our health security.”

Stakeholders at the meeting emphasized the need to strengthen community-based surveillance and ensure the rapid sharing of health information. The participating countries committed to translating agreements into concrete actions and making preparedness a political priority.

The Central African Republic highlighted that a mobile laboratory has been deployed in Obo, near the borders with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. The team on the ground is conducting enhanced surveillance, with a particular focus on community engagement and participation, as well as best practices for infection prevention and control.

The meeting, marked by calls for solidarity and cross-border cooperation, is expected to result in a joint roadmap and common action protocols.

fields.title: HCR TCHAD | Rapport opérationnel hebdomadaire du 15 aout 2026
fields.body:
**Réponse d’urgence à l’Est**

Le Tchad continue d’accueillir des réfugiés soudanais en quête de sécurité. Entre le 1er et le 15 août 2026, 2 373 nouveaux réfugiés soudanais ont été enregistrés dans les provinces de l’Ouaddaï, du Wadi Fira et de l’Ennedi Est, portant à plus de 941 700 le nombre total de réfugiés soudanais accueillis au Tchad depuis le début du conflit en avril 2023. Les nouveaux arrivants ont fui les violences persistantes, l’insécurité et les attaques contre les infrastructures civiles au Darfour. Fidèle à sa tradition d’accueil et au principe de nonrefoulement, le Gouvernement du Tchad a continué de garantir l’accès au territoire et à la protection internationale. Le HCR et ses partenaires ont poursuivi les activités d’enregistrement, de suivi de protection, de relocalisation et d’assistance vitale afin de répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables. Bien que les arrivées demeurent inférieures aux pics observés précédemment, le flux continu de réfugiés continue de peser sur les services de protection et les capacités de réponse humanitaire dans l’est du pays.

La relocalisation des réfugiés soudanais se poursuit malgré des capacités d’accueil sous forte pression. Entre le 1er et le 15 août 2026, le HCR et ses partenaires ont relocalisé 2 851 réfugiés soudanais (814 ménages), dont 561 personnes à besoins spécifiques, vers le site d’Arkoum dans l’est du Tchad. Depuis avril 2026, 33 900 réfugiés ont ainsi été transférés vers des sites d’accueil plus sûrs, portant le total des relocalisations à plus de 651 800 personnes depuis le début de la crise soudanaise. Ces mouvements demeurent essentiels pour réduire les risques de protection et améliorer l’accès aux services de base. Toutefois, la réponse reste confrontée à d’importants défis, notamment un déficit de 3 200 abris, la présence de 12 658 réfugiés en attente de relocalisation à Oure-Cassoni et la disponibilité limitée de nouveaux espaces d’accueil. En parallèle, le HCR a poursuivi les activités de préenregistrement, d’évaluation et de documentation des réfugiés, tout en soutenant la construction de 10 542 abris d’urgence pour les nouveaux arrivants.

Le HCR renforce simultanément l’assistance d’urgence et les solutions durables pour les réfugiés dans l’est du Tchad. Face aux impacts des fortes pluies, le HCR et ses partenaires ont poursuivi les évaluations des dommages, la réhabilitation des abris endommagés et l’appui aux ménages les plus vulnérables afin de répondre aux besoins urgents des populations réfugiées. Parallèlement, les initiatives en faveur de la protection de l’environnement et de l’accès à une énergie plus durable ont été intensifiées, avec la distribution de 23 875 plants, de plus de 4 800 foyers améliorés et le lancement de la distribution de charbon écologique à Goudrane. Des évaluations techniques ont également été réalisées pour rétablir le système solaire d’Iridimi, endommagé par les intempéries. Ces actions contribuent à renforcer la résilience des réfugiés et des communautés hôtes tout en favorisant des solutions plus durables face aux défis climatiques et environnementaux.

**Programme pour les personnes réfugiées.**

Le Gouvernement tchadien et ses partenaires renforcent la riposte au choléra dans les zones à risque. Face à la résurgence de cas de choléra dans certaines régions du pays, le Gouvernement tchadien, avec l’appui de ses partenaires, a intensifié les efforts de prévention et de réponse, notamment à travers la vaccination de plus de 700 000 personnes et le ciblage de 160 922 personnes supplémentaires dans les zones les plus exposées. Après la notification de nouveaux cas dans la province du Lac le 8 août, une équipe d’intervention rapide a été déployée à Haïrom et les mécanismes de surveillance transfrontalière ont été renforcés afin de limiter les risques de propagation.

Plus de 890 réfugiés et membres des communautés hôtes bénéficient d’un appui en cash pour renforcer leurs moyens de subsistance dans le sud du Tchad. Dans le cadre du projet financé par la Fondation Mastercard, le HCR et ses partenaires ont fourni une assistance monétaire à 892 réfugiés et membres des communautés hôtes, soit 81 % des 1 099 personnes ciblées. Au total, 102,5 millions de FCFA ont été distribués pour soutenir les activités agricoles et le réapprovisionnement en petit bétail, contribuant au renforcement de la sécurité alimentaire et de l’autonomie économique des ménages. En parallèle, huit groupements ont bénéficié d’un appui à la production de semences résilientes au climat et de fourrage, favorisant des moyens de subsistance plus durables et une meilleure résilience face aux chocs climatiques.

fields.title: HCR TCHAD | Rapport opérationnel hebdomadaire du 31 juillet 2026
fields.body:
**Réponse d’urgence à l’Est**

Le Tchad continue d’accueillir des réfugiés soudanais malgré un contexte régional instable. Depuis le déclenchement du conflit au Soudan en avril 2023, plus de 939 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile soudanais ont trouvé refuge au Tchad, principalement dans les provinces de l’Ouaddaï, du Wadi Fira, du Sila et de l’Ennedi Est. Les arrivées se sont poursuivies tout au long du mois de juillet 2026, avec 1 163 nouveaux arrivants enregistrés entre le 20 et le 26 juillet. Bien que le rythme des arrivées ait diminué par rapport au pic observé en janvier 2026, les déplacements restent étroitement liés à l’évolution de la situation sécuritaire au Darfour, la majorité des réfugiés entrant par les points frontaliers d’Adré et de Tiné. Cet afflux prolongé continue d’exercer une forte pression sur les capacités d’accueil, d’enregistrement, de protection et de fourniture des services essentiels, tandis que les besoins humanitaires demeurent supérieurs aux ressources disponibles. Toute détérioration de la situation au Darfour pourrait entraîner une nouvelle augmentation des mouvements de population vers l’est du Tchad.

Le HCR intensifie les relocalisations des réfugiés depuis la frontière vers des sites plus sûrs. Entre le 13 et le 26 juillet 2026, le HCR et ses partenaires ont relocalisé 2 996 réfugiés soudanais, dont 188 personnes ayant des besoins spécifiques, de la zone frontalière d’Adré vers le site d’Arkoum. Depuis le début de la crise en avril 2023, plus de 646 000 réfugiés ont ainsi été relocalisés vers des sites aménagés, dont plus de 18 600 depuis mars 2026. Ces relocalisations constituent une intervention de protection essentielle, permettant d’améliorer la sécurité des réfugiés et leur accès aux services de base. Toutefois, plus de 200 000 réfugiés demeurent à Adré, où la forte pression sur les infrastructures et les services, aggravées à d’importants déficits de financement, continue de limiter les capacités d’accueil et de ralentir les efforts de relocalisation.

L’est du Tchad reste confronté à d’importants défis en matière d’eau, d’hygiène et d’assainissement. Malgré les efforts en cours pour renforcer l’accès aux services EHA/WASH, la situation demeure préoccupante dans plusieurs sites de réfugiés, notamment à Oure-Cassoni. Au 25 juillet, seuls 4,4 litres d’eau par personne et par jour étaient disponibles, tandis qu’une latrine était partagée par 89 personnes, des niveaux bien en deçà des normes d’urgence. La croissance continue de la population réfugiée, combinée à des infrastructures insuffisantes, à des actes de vandalisme récurrents et à un engagement limité des partenaires, continue de peser sur les capacités de réponse. Parallèlement, l’Assistance Basée sur la Vulnérabilité (ABV) a couvert 255 836 ménages réfugiés, soit 81 % des 315 000 ménages ciblés dans les provinces du Ouaddaï, du Wadi Fira et du Sila. Cet exercice fournit des données essentielles pour mieux cibler les ménages les plus vulnérables, optimiser l’allocation des ressources limitées et renforcer l’efficacité ainsi que la redevabilité de la réponse humanitaire.

Réfugiés et communautés hôtes renforcent leur résilience face aux effets du changement climatique dans l’est du Tchad. Dans le cadre du projet financé par le Fonds vert pour le climat, le HCR, le PAM, les autorités locales et leurs partenaires poursuivent leurs efforts pour promouvoir une gestion durable des ressources naturelles dans les zones d’accueil des réfugiés. Entre le 22 et le 25 juillet, des activités de reboisement, de sensibilisation environnementale et de consultations communautaires ont mobilisé réfugiés et communautés hôtes autour d’actions visant à renforcer la résilience climatique et la cohésion sociale. Soutenues par la mise à disposition de 48 000 plants, ces initiatives contribuent à l’adaptation au changement climatique, à la restauration des écosystèmes dégradés et à la promotion de solutions durables au bénéfice des populations déplacées et des communautés locales.

fields.title: Dans le canton de Donia (province du Logone Oriental), réfugiés et communautés hôtes construisent une nouvelle dynamique locale avec l’appui du HCR et de l’Union européenne
fields.body:
Par Aristophane Ngargoune

Assistant Communications Officer

• HCR N’Djaména

**Goré, 14 août 2026** – « Ces réfugiés sont nos frères. Nous partagions déjà les mêmes traditions. Je crois que leur présence dans notre village va booster notre économie locale » confie Silas, tout souriant un jeune Tchadien la trentaine, présent à l’arrivée des réfugiés centrafricains fin juin 2026 dans son village de Betembo, dans le canton de Donia après leur installation volontaire dans le cadre d’une initiative visant à favoriser leur autonomie et leur inclusion au sein des communautés hôtes. Les nouveaux arrivants ont été accueillis dans une ferveur suivant la tradition d’hospitalité profondément ancrées au Sud du Tchad, marquée par des salutations, l’ouverture et la disponibilité, le partage de nourriture et de boissons, l’assistance spontanée.

L’installation volontaire des réfugiés centrafricains dans le canton de Donia, dans la province du Logone Oriental, s’inscrit dans le cadre du Projet d’Alternative aux Camps et de Résilience Agricole au Sud du Tchad (PACRAS) financé par l’Union européenne et lancé à Donia le 17 février 2026.

Le projet vise à accompagner les réfugiés et les communautés hôtes vers une plus grande autonomie et une meilleure inclusion économique et des solutions moins dépendantes de l’aide humanitaire. Un premier groupe de 110 familles réfugiées a volontairement quitté les sites aménagés de Goré (Amboko, Gondje, Doholo et Dosseye) après avoir reçu du cash pour leur transport, pour aller s’installer dans les villages de Betembo et Doborote les 29 et 30 juin 2026.

Dimanche Salomon, réfugié, venu du site aménage de Dossey (où il y était établi depuis 2007) et installé volontairement dans le village Betembo se réjouit de sa nouvelle vie hors du camp. « Nous serons respectueux des principes locaux. Ensemble, Tchadiens et réfugiés, nous travailleront pour cultiver les terres, accroître la production agricole et commercialiser les récoltes sur le marché local » confit-il.

Pour accompagner cette dynamique, l’ONG Initiative Humanitaire pour le Développement Local (IHDL) partenaire du HCR, a organisé durant la dernière semaine de juin la distribution de matériels agricoles à la population autochtone de Donia. Cette distribution s’était aussi étendue aux réfugiés aussitôt installés dans les villages d’accueils.

Des unités de culture attelée, des charrues et des jougs ont été remis aux producteurs locaux et réfugiés afin de renforcer leurs capacités de production, améliorer les techniques culturales et accroître les rendements agricoles dans les zones concernées par le projet.

À l’issue de cette dotation, le chef de canton de Donia, sa majesté Takoral Rodrigue a réaffirmé sa satisfaction pour ce projet qui contribue aussi à promouvoir une agriculture plus productive et à favoriser l’autonomisation économique des deux communautés. « Nous avions toujours accueilli des réfugiés à Donia. La cohabitation pacifique et le vivre ensemble dans le respect réciproque seront des atouts pour ce projet qui sera très bénéfique pour le canton Donia » témoigne-t-il.

En soutenant la génération de revenus et les activités économiques partagées, le projet contribuera au dynamisme de l’économie locale et à la promotion d’une coexistence pacifique.

Ces deux activités ont vu une forte présence des autorités administratives et traditionnelles, des partenaires du projet ainsi que des réfugiés et la communauté hôte.

Au-delà du soutien aux activités agricoles, PACRAS permettra de renforcer les services publics essentiels dans les cinq villages qui accueilleront les réfugiés. Les centres de santé, les écoles, les systèmes d’approvisionnement en eau et les infrastructures d’assainissement bénéficieront d’un appui afin de répondre aux besoins d’une population élargie.

fields.title: Ebola Outbreak: Regional Humanitarian Access Snapshot - August 2026
fields.body:
The Ebola outbreak is largely unfolding in eastern DRC, a region already facing acute humanitarian needs, where armed  
 conflict and mass displacement have significantly constrained humanitarian access, complicating response efforts,  
 and the delivery of life-saving assistance. Declared by WHO on 17 May 2026, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak is  
 increasingly affecting cross-border movements, including humanitarian and health workers, cargo, and commercial  
 travel.  
 Despite WHO guidance and risk assessments recommending open borders with adequate screening and monitoring at  
 points of entry, several countries have imposed movement restrictions. On 17 July 2026, the DRC replaced its blanket  
 21-day travel restriction with a risk-based approach: high-risk travellers face reinforced isolation and travel restrictions,  
 low-risk travellers undergo active monitoring and case-by-case travel clearance, while minimal-risk travellers self-monitor  
 without systematic restrictions.  
 Border controls along the DRC’s borders continue to constrain cross-border movement and humanitarian access,  
 disrupting established supply routes and straining regional logistics. The Bukavu-Uvira-Bujumbura corridor remains in  
 use despite security risks; humanitarian staff cross Lake Kivu by boat from Goma to Bukavu, then travel overland via  
 RN5, with advance notification required for the Bukavu-Uvira segment due to active frontlines. With Goma airport  
 closed and access to Bunia previously limited, Entebbe remains a critical humanitarian logistics hub. UNHAS operates  
 passenger and cargo flights from Entebbe to Bunia, supporting access to eastern DRC; however, the Bunia–Entebbe  
 route is not yet open to humanitarian staff.

fields.title: Note de plaidoyer: Pour Le renforcement de rapprentissage sur et protecteur en periode d'Ebola a ['Est de la Republique Dernocratique du Congo
fields.body:
**Introduction**

La présente note vise à mobiliser les autorités nationales et provinciales, les partenaires techniques et financiers, les agences des Nations Unies, les organisations humanitaires et les acteurs communautaires afin de garantir la continuité d’un apprentissage sûr, inclusif et protecteur pour les enfants affectés par l’épidémie d’Ebola dans l’Est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) en général et en Ituri, SudKivu, Nord-Kivu en particulier. Il est du devoir de tous de faire de l’école un espace à la fois d’apprentissage, de prévention, de protection, de soutien psychosocial et d’orientation vers les services essentiels, tout en réduisant les risques de transmission de la maladie à virus d’Ebola.

**Contexte et justification**

L’épidémie d’Ebola déclarée en RDC en mai 2026 intervient dans un contexte déjà marqué par les conflits armés, les déplacements de populations, la pauvreté, la faiblesse des infrastructures et la perturbation des services sociaux de base. Des sources concordantes locales soulignent que la réponse se déroule dans des zones caractérisées notamment par l’insécurité, les mouvements importants des populations et les difficultés d’accès, ce qui complique la surveillance, la prévention et la continuité des services essentiels.

Les enfants figurent parmi les populations les plus exposées aux conséquences directes et indirectes de l’épidémie. En juin 2026, l’UNICEF estimait qu’environ 2,95 millions d’enfants et d’adolescents de moins de 18 ans, représentant 54 % de la population des 51 zones de santé touchées, étaient exposés aux risques liés à Ebola et à la perturbation des services essentiels. Plus de 150 enfants sont déjà devenus orphelins dans la province de l’Ituri.

En mai 2026, le Cluster Education province de l’Ituri dans a estimé que 834 écoles(295434 élèves dont 150830 filles et 144604 Garçons et 12450 enseignants) avec seulement 160 points d’eaux dont la moitié ne fonctionne pas pour les zones à risque de Rwampara, Bunia, Nizi et Kilo sont exposées aux risque graves de la maladie à Viris Ebala qui entrave le système éducatif de la province et un taux de la déperdition de 30% pourrait être observé pour l’année scolaire 2025-2026 dans la province de l’Ituri.

A environ 3 semaines de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, la crise sanitaire risque également d'accentuer les interruptions de scolarité, l’abandon scolaire, la détresse psychosociale, la stigmatisation des enfants et familles affectés, ainsi que les risques de protection, notamment pour les filles, les enfants séparés ou non accompagnés et les enfants vivant dans des ménages déplacés. Les membres de groupes et les plateformes d’hommes impliquées dans l’éveil communautaire soulignent que les épidémies d’Ebola perturbent simultanément les services de santé, de nutrition, d’éducation et de protection de l’enfance.

Dans ce contexte, la fermeture prolongée des écoles ne doit pas constituer la seule réponse. Il est nécessaire d’investir dans des mesures permettant de maintenir ou de reprendre l’apprentissage dans des conditions adaptées au niveau de risque épidémiologique. ActionAid sous le financement d’ECHO met notamment en œuvre des actions de prévention et de contrôle des infections dans 140 écoles en appuyant directement 42,000 élèves du primaire, les communautés et les établissements de santé des Zones de Santé de l’Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu et Maniema.

fields.title: Disease Outbreak News: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo & Uganda (14 August 2026)
fields.body:
**Situation at a glance**

The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is in a phase of intense transmission. It is the largest Ebola outbreak ever reported in the country and expanding faster than any previous Ebola outbreak. The epidemic is increasingly characterized by sustained transmission within interconnected geographic clusters. Initially confined to the Mongbwalu health zone in Ituri Province, the outbreak has now expanded to 54 health zones across six provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and Bas-Uélé). The most recently affected Bas-Uélé province recorded one confirmed case in Buta health zone with travel history to Haut-Uélé and onset of symptoms on 4 August. As of 12 August 2026, a total of 4665 confirmed cases, including 2184 deaths, have been reported, corresponding to a crude case fatality ratio (CFR) of 46.8%. The ongoing rise in cases, broader geographic spread, and continued high mortality demonstrate the rapidly changing scope of this public health emergency of international concern. During the most recent reporting week (epidemiological week 32, 3 to 9 August 2026), the highest weekly number of reported cases (579) and deaths (304) were recorded, highlighting the exceptional pace of transmission. The ongoing humanitarian crisis, compounded by insecurity, population displacement and mobility, and cross-border movements, continues to pose significant challenges to response efforts and increase the risk of further geographical spread. National authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, continue to implement extensive response measures in collaboration with WHO and partners. However, a substantial scaling up of response activities is underway to get ahead of the outbreak. Following their missions to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, WHO’s Director-General and Regional Director for Africa, and the Director General of Africa CDC, highlighted surveillance activities and closer work with communities as priority areas. Expanding the number of treatment centers, across more areas, is underway, along with training for the health and care workers to staff them. France has reported no secondary transmission following an imported case detected on 24 June 2026. As of 14 August, 41 days had passed since the patient’s discharge on 4 July, with no additional confirmed cases reported. In Uganda the most recent imported case was discharged from a treatment centre on 16 July, and the 42-day enhanced monitoring period will cease on 27 August. Uganda remains at risk of BVD re-introduction due to ongoing transmission in neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo and is undertaking heightened surveillance activities given continued population movement and the risk of cross-border transmission. A regional preparedness and prioritization framework continues to guide readiness and response activities across the African Region.

**Description of the situation**

Since the previous [Disease Outbreak News](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON614) was published on 1 August 2026, additional confirmed cases and deaths of BVD have been only reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Cumulatively as of 12 August 2026, 4686 confirmed cases have been reported: 4665 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (including two cases diagnosed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and subsequently treated in Germany), 20 in Uganda and one in France. A total of 2186 deaths have been reported, including two in Uganda. As of 12 August, at least 986 patients have recovered including 965 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 18 from Uganda have recovered, two in Germany and one from France.

As reported in the [Disease Outbreak News](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON614) published on 1 August 2026, with more confirmed cases than the 2018-2020 outbreak, which reported 3,317 cases, this outbreak now represents the largest Ebola disease outbreak ever documented in the country.

**Democratic Republic of the Congo**

Since 1 August 2026 when the last Disease Outbreak News was published, an additional 1060 confirmed cases, including 597 confirmed deaths, have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The increase is in part due to strengthened surveillance activities, enhanced laboratory testing, and diagnostic capacity. However, most of the increase reflects the expansion of the outbreak.

As of 12 August 2026, a total of 4665 confirmed cases, including 2184 deaths (CFR 46.8%), have been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. To date, 965 patients have recovered.

Cases have been reported from 54 health zones (HZ) across six provinces: Ituri (28/36 HZ), North Kivu (12/34 HZ), South Kivu (1/34 HZ), Haut-Uélé (6/13 HZ), Tshopo (6/23 HZ), and Bas- Uélé (1/11 HZ). The most recently affected province, Bas-Uélé, reported one confirmed case in Buta Health Zone. The case had a travel history to Haut-Uélé, with symptom onset on 4 August.

As of 12 August, of the 54 affected health zones, 100 new confirmed cases were reported in the last 24 hours from 22 health zones in all affected provinces except for Sud-Kivu. The highest number of new cases in the last 24 hours (67) was reported from Ituri province followed by Nord-Kivu (25). Ituri remains the most affected province, accounting for 85% (3979/4665) of all confirmed cases and 79% (1726/2184) of reported deaths nationwide.

As of 12 August, the proportion of contacts followed up in the last 24 hours is at 84.2% (17 460 seen out of 20 740 to follow up).

As of 9 August, infections among health workers continue, with at least 155 confirmed cases, including 45 deaths (CFR: 29%) and 68 recoveries since beginning of the outbreak. These infections highlight ongoing occupational exposure risks, persistent challenges in implementing infection prevention and control (IPC) in health-care facilities—especially outside of the designated Ebola treatment centres which have more established protocols and access to supplies--and continued exposure risk in the community.

The outbreak is taking place amid a severe humanitarian crisis and ongoing insecurity, characterized by large-scale population displacement, significant population mobility, and constrained access to critical services, including health care, safe water, food, shelter, and protection. Response efforts in the affected provinces have been hindered by insecurity and attacks on health facilities, which have curtailed access for response teams, discouraging potential patients from seeking care, disrupting surveillance and response activities and increasing the risk of undetected transmission. Since the declaration of the Ebola public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) [on 17 May 2026](https://www.who.int/news/item/22-05-2026-first-meeting-of-the-ihr-emergency-committee-regarding-the-epidemic-of-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-disease-in-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-and-uganda-2026-temporary-recommendations), 12 attacks on health care have been recorded, with additional reports under verification. These challenges underscore the importance of community-centred response efforts led by local authorities and trusted community leaders.

**Epidemiology**

Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus, one of the Orthoebolavirus species. It is a zoonotic disease, with fruit bats suspected to be the natural reservoir.

Human infection is thought to occur through close contact with the blood or secretions of infected wildlife, such as bats or non-human primates, and it subsequently spreads from person-to-person through direct contact with the blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected individuals or contaminated surfaces and materials. Transmission is particularly amplified in health-care settings when IPC measures are inadequate and during unsafe burial practices involving direct contact with deceased individuals.

The incubation period for BVD ranges from two to 21 days, and infected individuals are not infectious until symptom onset. Early symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, and sore throat are non-specific, which complicates clinical diagnosis and can delay detection. These symptoms then progress to gastrointestinal symptoms, organ dysfunction, and, in some cases, haemorrhagic manifestations.

CFRs in the past two BVD outbreaks, reported in Uganda and in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2007 and 2012, were 30% and 50%, respectively.

Differentiating BVD from other endemic febrile illnesses such as malaria is challenging without laboratory confirmation using PCR or antigen- or antibody-based assays. Outbreak control relies on rapid case identification, isolation and care, contact tracing, safe burials and strong community engagement, as no approved vaccines or specific treatments currently exist for BVD.

**Public health response**

For detailed information about the ongoing public health response actions by the respective Ministry of Health, WHO and partners please refer to the latest situation reports published by the WHO Regional Office for Africa: [Ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo | WHO | Regional Office for Africa](https://www.afro.who.int/health-topics/ebola-disease/outbreak-drc-26) | WHO| Regional Office for Africa

Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, in collaboration with WHO and partners, are continuing to implementing extensive public health measures, including the continental preparedness and response plan, a strategic six-month framework plan designed to guide coordinated efforts to strengthen outbreak response measures, including emergency coordination, disease surveillance, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control, clinical care, community engagement, research, logistics and support for essential health services, engaging donors and mobilizing additional resources to address critical funding gaps and sustain response operations across affected and at-risk areas. A substantial scale-up is ongoing across all response pillars to get ahead of the outbreak.

**WHO risk assessment**

On 6 June 2026, WHO reassessed the risk of the outbreak of BVD to incorporate newly available information and align with the WHO [Temporary Recommendations](https://www.who.int/news/item/22-05-2026-first-meeting-of-the-ihr-emergency-committee-regarding-the-epidemic-of-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-disease-in-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-and-uganda-2026-temporary-recommendations). The risk for countries sharing land borders with countries with documented Bundibugyo virus detection, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda at the time of assessment, was separated from the risk for other countries in the African Region.

The risk in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was assessed as very high due to ongoing transmission and the continued expansion of the outbreak into new health zones, increasing the potential for further national and regional spread.

The risk in Uganda was assessed as high due to confirmed cross-border spread through imported cases and ongoing epidemiological links along the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo–western Uganda corridor, which has historically been affected by Ebola outbreaks, including Bundibugyo virus and Sudan virus disease.

The risk for countries sharing land borders with countries reporting BDBV detection was assessed as high due to sustained population mobility linked to cross-border trade and mining activities, variation in capacities and experience of BVD response, and variable levels of readiness.

The risk for the rest of the African region and at the global level was assessed as low.

An updated Rapid Risk Assessment is being developed in advance of the upcoming IHR Emergency Committee meeting regarding the epidemic of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo scheduled for 18 August. This is the second meeting of the committee, following their initial meeting after the Director-General characterized the situation as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May 2026.

**WHO advice**

Based on the currently available information, WHO advises against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries. WHO continues to closely monitor and, where necessary, verify travel and trade measures in relation to this event.

For further information on the considerations for implementing border health and international travel-related temporary recommendations, please see the relevant [technical note issued on 26 May 2026](https://iris.who.int/items/b07def43-df30-41b8-83e0-deb33bcfd697).

The [Temporary Recommendations](https://www.who.int/news/item/22-05-2026-first-meeting-of-the-ihr-emergency-committee-regarding-the-epidemic-of-ebola-bundibugyo-virus-disease-in-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-and-uganda-2026-temporary-recommendations) issued to States Parties on 22 May 2026 underscore the importance of coordinated outbreak control, strengthened cross‑border collaboration, and sustained surveillance and preparedness to prevent further regional spread and ensure an effective public health response.

Rapid recognition of cases, testing and optimized supportive care can reduce mortality, and improve community perceptions and acceptance of health care within the response.

WHO has convened several technical advisory groups, including the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE) to assess candidate vaccines and therapeutics for BVD.

On 7 August, the WHO Technical Advisory Group released a report regarding possible candidate vaccines for Bundibugyo virus disease. The members recommended that Ervebo, the only licensed Ebola vaccine (previously known as ebolavirus Zaire), be prioritized for inclusion in a randomized clinical trial in the context of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo WHO is working with partners to start this trial as soon as possible.

In addition, WHO is sponsoring a clinical trial to find effective treatments against BVD. The trial began enrollment on 2 July. The trial, known as the PARTNERS trial, is now open in three different clinical management facilities in Ituri province and has enrolled over 100 confirmed cases.

fields.title: IOM: Multi-Country Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak - Situation Report No. 13 (3-9 August 2026)
fields.body:
According to the World Health Organization, as of 10 August, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported 4,449 confirmed cases of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (BVD), including 2,061 deaths.

With the recent increase in reported cases, the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak has become the largest and fastest-growing outbreak ever reported in DRC. The rapidly escalating outbreak is unfolding against the backdrop of an ongoing triple crisis in eastern DRC, where health risks, large-scale displacement and persistent conflict intersect. Displaced populations living in camps face complex and multidimensional needs requiring coordinated, multisectoral interventions. Across affected areas, most deaths continue to occur within communities, underscoring the urgent need to strengthen contact tracing and community event-based surveillance to support earlier detection, referral and response.

The spread of the outbreak into Tshopo and Haut-Uélé Provinces underscores continued need to comprehensively address the mobility dimensions of the ongoing public health response. While no positive Ebola case has been reported on vessels arriving via riverine routes in Kinshasa, heightened transmission risks require strengthened coordination and vigilance at points of control (PoCs) along the river to prevent further geographic spread. In parallel, the rising number of cases in Haut-Uélé requires enhanced disease surveillance and cross-border coordination to prevent disease transmission into neighbouring South Sudan and the Central African Republic (CAR).

During the reporting period, key highlights include :

- **4,449 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,061 deaths** in the DRC as of 10 August 2026, making this the **largest and fastest-growing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country**.
- Over **16.5 million health screenings** supported at **225 points** of entry and points of control across affected and at-risk countries.
- During the reporting period, IOM supported **2.57 million health screenings in the DRC alone**
- More than **13.1 million individuals reached** through risk communication and community engagement activities.
- Trained **575 health workers in Rwanda** on Ebola detection, infection prevention and control, surveillance, and response measures.
- Continued to strengthen surveillance and preparedness capacities along critical mobility corridors, including riverine routes into Kinshasa and border areas near South Sudan and the Central African Republic.

The outbreak continues to unfold in a complex operational environment marked by insecurity, displacement, and population mobility. As transmission persists in eastern DRC, sustained investment in surveillance, border health measures, community engagement, and support to displaced and mobile populations remains critical to containing the outbreak and preventing cross-border spread. [Learn more HERE](https://crisisresponse.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl1481/files/uploaded-files/IOM-Multi-Country-Bundibugyo-virus-disease-Response-Sit-Rep-No-13-3-9-August-2026.pdf)

Plusieurs flambées épidémiques touchent actuellement le continent africain. Ebola en République démocratique du Congo, choléra dans l’État du Borno au Nigéria, Mpox dans plusieurs pays : derrière ces épidémies, des facteurs communs fragilisent les populations et compliquent la réponse sanitaire.

Déplacements de population, accès limité à l’eau potable, systèmes de santé fragilisés ou encore difficultés d’accès humanitaire : les contextes de crise peuvent favoriser la propagation des maladies et compliquer la détection et la prise en charge des cas. Face à ces épidémies, les enjeux de prévention, de surveillance et d’accès aux soins restent essentiels.

fields.title: Three months into the Ebola outbreak: Overcoming local resistance, Red Cross volunteers stand by their communities by building trust as the virus continues to spread | IFRC
fields.body:
**Trust at the heart of the response**

As the outbreak evolves, the Red Cross response is adapting.

Despite these immense challenges, approximately 1,500 DRC Red Cross volunteers remain mobilized on the front lines of the response. Since the outbreak was declared, their vital work has enabled **1,400 safe and dignified burials** to help break chains of transmission, while more than **240,000 people** have been reached with life-saving information to counter rumours and misinformation.

Behind these figures are thousands of interactions in which trust can determine whether an alert is reported, whether a family accepts a safe and dignified burial, or whether potentially life-saving information is believed.

Between 26 July-8 August teams collected **3895 pieces of community feedback**, which included persistent rumours about an alleged ***“Ebola business”***, conspiracy theories and mistrust of response teams.

Ushindi, a 48-year-old motorcycle taxi driver and Red Cross volunteer for 16 years, was attacked alongside Dieudonné. He had heard rumours accusing the Red Cross, among others, of being responsible for the spread of Ebola, without imagining just how dangerous those rumours could become.

The attack left him with partial paralysis of his right hand, balance problems and severe insomnia. He has been unable to return to his work as a motorcycle taxi driver. And yet, he returned to join the other volunteers.

**Scaling up the response to keep pace with the outbreak**

In affected areas, DRC Red Cross teams, supported by the IFRC and its partners, are working across multiple fronts: awareness campaigns, community-based surveillance, safe and dignified burials, infection prevention and control, and mental health and psychosocial support.

Additional resources are also reaching frontline teams. Three containers received in early August carried more than [19 tonnes of humanitarian supplies, including 23 safe and dignified burial kits, 8,000 body bags and more than 2,000 units of alcohol-based hand rub](https://www.ifrc.org/press-release/ifrc-scales-ebola-response-drc-critical-supplies-reach-frontline-teams).

But as the outbreak continues to expand, the response envisioned in May must now be scaled up.

fields.title: DRC: Cholera, measles, and malaria health emergencies must not be forgotten during Ebola disease outbreak
fields.body:
13 August 2026 - While the response to the Ebola disease outbreak is mobilising significant resources in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Médecins Sans Frontières / Doctors Without Borders (MSF) warns of the need to maintain care and funding for other health crises in the east of the country to prevent a worsening of the humanitarian situation. Cholera, measles, malaria and violence linked to the ongoing conflict, among others, continue to threaten thousands of people in North and South Kivu.

Since the Ebola disease outbreak was declared in May, media attention and resources have focused largely on the response to this emergency. While this mobilisation is essential to contain the outbreak, it must not come at the expense of other health and humanitarian needs that persist in North and South Kivu.

*“The Ebola disease outbreak is a major emergency, but it is not the only one. Every day, we receive patients suffering from various diseases, people injured in fighting, and survivors of sexual violence. For these communities, all these emergencies coexist and require a simultaneous response. When basic healthcare is interrupted, more people risk dying from preventable diseases. It is essential to preserve continuity of care and access to primary healthcare in order to treat all other conditions,”* explains Joshua Eckley, MSF Head of Programmes in South Kivu.

While the Ebola disease outbreak is the focus of attention, other outbreaks are spreading in Eastern DRC. According to official data, more than 108,643 suspected measles cases, with 1,394 deaths, were reported across the country from January to 19 July 2026. **Nearly half of these cases — more than 50,827 — are concentrated in North and South Kivu.** At the same time, the country has already recorded more than 35,464 suspected cholera cases and more than 1,051 deaths. Of these notifications, 14,819 are concentrated in the two provinces.

MSF has mobilised in the fight against measles in North and South Kivu. Teams have carried out six interventions in response to measles outbreaks. The most recent are still ongoing, taking place in Shabunda, South Kivu, and Walikale, North Kivu. Together, these interventions have already made it possible to treat more than 12,050 patients and vaccinate more than 283,150 children.

At the same time, teams are facing a worrying resurgence of cholera. In Bukavu and Shabunda, South Kivu, MSF continues to care for patients following a surge in cases recorded last year in the province. In Goma, teams were also mobilised to tackle a cholera outbreak between May and early August 2026. In total, more than 2,410 people with cholera have already been treated in MSF-supported facilities.

*“For the families we care for, there is no hierarchy between crises. Whether a child dies of measles or malaria, whether a person succumbs to cholera or Ebola disease, every life matters,”* says Dr Yvan Mbangi, MSF Deputy Medical Coordinator in Goma.

Beyond its response to Ebola disease, measles and cholera outbreaks, MSF continues to provide essential healthcare in Masisi, Mweso, Walikale, Bambo, Kibirizi, Kirotshe, Goma and Rutshuru in North Kivu, and in Minova, Bunyakiri and Uvira in South Kivu. But given the scale of the needs, this mobilisation remains largely inadequate. These crises require a much greater commitment from health authorities and humanitarian actors to guarantee access to care for the most vulnerable populations.

**Do not push other crises into the background**

While humanitarian needs continue to increase, available funding is decreasing. [**North Kivu could notably be excluded from the next three-year Global Fund funding cycle dedicated to the fight against malaria.**](https://www.msf.org/fr/rdcongo/msf-alerte-sur-l%E2%80%99exclusion-du-nord-kivu-du-prochain-cycle-de-financement-du-fonds-mondial)

Yet malaria remains the leading cause of morbidity in DRC, including in North Kivu. Population displacement caused by fighting forces many families to seek refuge in forests or isolated areas, where exposure to mosquitoes is greater and access to healthcare is particularly limited.

*“We risk seeing a reduction in the resources dedicated to the disease that nevertheless kills the most people in this region. It would be a tragic paradox: mobilising considerable resources against one outbreak while weakening the response to a disease that continues to cause a far higher number of deaths every day,”* warns Dr Mbangi.

Years of conflict, massive population displacement and chronic insecurity, as well as the drastic reduction in humanitarian aid funding, have drastically weakened the health system in North and South Kivu. Many health centres and hospitals are operating with reduced capacity due to a lack of staff, medicines and equipment, while others have had to suspend their activities because of violence. In several areas, hundreds of thousands of people remain without regular access to healthcare.

*“While medical-humanitarian needs continue to grow in eastern DRC, we call on the authorities, donors and all humanitarian actors to maintain and strengthen their investments in all responses to the many and diverse needs of the population. It is vital that all emergencies be addressed simultaneously,”* concludes Joshua Eckley.
